rootCauses.title: Inserting a node created in one frame/realm into another frame's document COPIES it: the original loses its parent and the challenge's later parentNode.replaceChild() throws
rootCauses.area: crates/script/js/20_dom.js (adoptForeign ~L821, L.adoptArg ~L853, preInsert ~L858, insertCore, adoptNode ~L2914-2926); crates/script/src (N.foreignNodeType, per-frame realms/documents)
rootCauses.mechanism: Each frame has its own realm and document (README 'Frame windows'). When a node from another realm is passed to appendChild/insertBefore/replaceChild/append, L.adoptArg -> adoptForeign (20_dom.js:821-853) round-trips it through `template.innerHTML = o.outerHTML`, removes the original from its old parent and inserts the COPY. So `ret = iframeBody.appendChild(x)` returns a different object (ret !== x), and x.parentNode === null, x.ownerDocument unchanged, x.isConnected === false, layout/rect calls on x see a detached node. In Chromium adoption MOVES the same node (x.parentNode === iframeBody, x.ownerDocument === iframeDoc, x is the same object even though x instanceof iframeWindow.Node is true and x instanceof Node is false). The Turnstile iframe does exactly this in its SVG-text/font-metrics probe: it creates a placeholder <div> with the challenge document, appends it into the blank helper <iframe>'s body, imports the <template> content (document.importNode) and then runs `ph.parentNode.replaceChild(imported, ph)`; in Sharko ph.parentNode is null -> `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replaceChild')` (VM handler 'az', reported to Cloudflare through the /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/b/eb/.../chl_api_m beacon). The same failure also makes the following getBBox()/getComputedTextLength()/getExtentOfChar() calls act on detached nodes.
evidence: MITM proxy between Sharko and the sandbox proxy (SHARKO_EXTRA_CA + injected prelude that hooks JSON.stringify(Error) = the challenge's error reporter): every run on leo.org, codepen.io, gutefrage.net, medium.com prints `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replaceChild')` from the turnstile iframe script and sends 2 POST /eb/.../chl_api_m beacons; Chromium behind the same proxy with the same prelude: 0 errors, 0 /eb/ beacons.

API trace of the iframe (trace_sharko.txt vs trace_chromium.txt): right before the error `HTMLDocument.importNode(DocumentFragment,true) => DocumentFragment` then `<div>.parentNode [get] => null conn=false`; Chromium never reads a null parentNode in that frame.

repro.html (below): iframeBody.appendChild(document.createElement('div')) -> Chromium {ret_is_ph:true,parent_is_ibody:true,ownerIsIframeDoc:true,connected:true,replace:'ok'}; Sharko {ret_is_ph:false,parent_is_ibody:false,parentName:'null',ownerIsIframeDoc:false,connected:false,replace:"ERR Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replaceChild')"}. insertBefore and append() behave the same.
Same-realm control (node created by iframeDoc.createElement) works in Sharko: only the cross-realm path is broken.

repro.expected: Chromium: appended node keeps identity, parentNode === iframe body, isConnected true, ph.parentNode.replaceChild(...) works
repro.actual: Sharko: appendChild returns a copy, original has parentNode null / not connected, replaceChild throws TypeError

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high - every Cloudflare managed challenge / Turnstile runs this probe, and any page that builds DOM in the parent and inserts it into an iframe document (editors, ads, sandboxed previews, CodePen-style runners, recaptcha helpers) hits the same identity loss.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Make adoption move the node instead of copying it. Preferred: when a node of realm A is inserted into a document of realm B, move the native subtree into B's document (native call that transfers node ids between the two frames' documents) and REBIND the existing JS wrapper of realm A to the new (docB, id) so the same object stays valid (ownerDocument/parentNode/isConnected/getBoundingClientRect/mutation all resolve through the new binding; the wrapper keeps realm A's prototype chain, exactly like Chromium where `x instanceof B.Node` is true). Interim if the arenas cannot be merged: keep the copy but turn the ORIGINAL wrapper into a forwarding handle to the copy after insertion (store `forward = copyWrapper` in a WeakMap consulted by idOf()/parentNode/ownerDocument/isConnected/getRootNode/contains/childNodes/attributes/style/getBoundingClientRect/getBBox), and make the return value of appendChild/insertBefore/replaceChild/append the ORIGINAL argument. Same for Document.adoptNode/importNode of foreign nodes (20_dom.js:2914-2926). Add a WPT-style test: tests for 'iframe.contentDocument.body.appendChild(parentDoc.createElement("div"))' identity and parent.

rootCauses.title: Shadow DOM approximation detaches the light-DOM children of a shadow host: after body.attachShadow() nothing appended to <body> (and even the pre-existing children) is connected/findable
rootCauses.area: crates/script/js/20_dom.js (attachShadowImpl ~L246, shadowPrepare ~L214 (moves the host's children into a detached `lightFrag`), shadowDistribute ~L221, preInsert ~L858 / lightInsert ~L875, clearShadowContent), vendor/blitz-dom (no flat tree, only setShadowHost style scoping)
rootCauses.mechanism: The shadow root shares the HOST's native node id (comment at 20_dom.js:245-249): shadow content is stored as the host's native children and the real light children are parked in a hidden detached fragment (`info.lightFrag`), only re-inserted into a matching <slot>. Consequences that violate the DOM contract: host.appendChild(x)/insertAdjacentHTML/innerHTML/append land in lightFrag -> x.parentNode is a #document-fragment (not the host), x.isConnected === false, host.childNodes/children/lastChild do not contain x, document.getElementById / querySelector(All) cannot see x, an <iframe> appended there has contentDocument === null, and the children the host had before attachShadow (e.g. <div id=pre>) disappear from document.getElementById. Also node.compareDocumentPosition(hostshadowNode) returns 20 (contained-by) instead of 37 (disconnected/implementation-specific) and host.contains(shadowNode) is true (Chromium false). The Turnstile iframe calls `document.body.attachShadow({mode:'closed'})` as one of its first steps and then runs its font/CSS-property fingerprint by `document.body.appendChild(document.createElement(null))` (a <null> element), `nullEl.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend','<div id=crERV20 class=EBOl60 ...>')`, `document.querySelectorAll('#crERV20')[0]`. In Sharko the querySelectorAll result is empty, the VM then calls a method on `undefined` (its property-get helper returns the KEY string when the object is undefined, so the call fails as `TypeError: <reg> is not a function`; instrumented: CFGET-ONUNDEF key=insertAdjacentHTML) and the measurement is garbage/absent. Note Chromium itself renders nothing for unslotted light children but keeps them in the tree, so all script-visible behaviour above is observable there.
evidence: Trace of the iframe (prelude5): `<body>.attachShadow(Object) => ShadowRoot` is event #4; later `appendChild(<null>) into <body> this===document.body:true ... this.lastChild===c:false this.childNodes=2 c.connected=false c.parent=#document-fragment ... body children: STYLE,DIV` and `<null>.insertAdjacentHTML(...)`: connected=false, parent=#document-fragment, qsa(#crERV20)=0, getElementById=false.

Diff of ordered API traces Chromium vs Sharko: Chromium continues with 200 events of querySelectorAll('.EBOl6x')/insertAdjacentHTML/insertRule/getBoundingClientRect (font probe); Sharko has `NodeList.0 [get] => undef` and falls into another path.

VM instrumentation (property-get helper patched in the served script): `CFGET-ONUNDEF key=insertAdjacentHTML` (call on undefined = querySelectorAll(..)[0]) in the unpatched run; with a shim that redirects body.attachShadow to a child <div> this event disappears (but the two other TypeErrors remain, see other root cause).

repro.html: Chromium {isConnected:true,parentIsBody:true,bodyChildren:'5:div#pre,script,div#lightkid',gebi:true,qsa:1,iahFound:1,preFound:'true/true',cmp:37,contains:false}; Sharko {isConnected:false,parentName:'#document-fragment',bodyChildren:'1:div#inshadow',gebi:false,qsa:0,iahFound:0,preFound:'false/null',cmp:20,contains:true}. Same for a normal <div> host (probe_env 'shadow': Chromium true|true|1, Sharko false|false|0). A plain <unknown-el> without shadow root works in Sharko (repro_iah_plain_ok.html), so the failure is the shadow emulation, not insertAdjacentHTML.
repro_iframe_in_shadow.html: an <iframe> appended as light child of a shadowed body gets contentDocument/contentWindow null in Sharko (Chromium: normal doc).

repro.expected: Chromium: light children stay children of the host (isConnected true, parentNode === host, found by getElementById/querySelectorAll); shadow nodes are NOT contained by the host (compareDocumentPosition 37)
repro.actual: Sharko: light children go to a detached fragment (parentNode #document-fragment, isConnected false, not queryable); pre-existing light children vanish; shadow nodes reported as contained

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high - all Cloudflare Turnstile/managed challenges (millions of pages) and every web-component page whose host has light children (Lit, Shoelace, Stencil, custom widgets, cookie banners) lose light-DOM nodes from the document tree.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Stop moving light children into a detached fragment. Keep every light child a real native child of the host (so parentNode/isConnected/getRootNode/contains/document queries/insertAdjacentHTML work), and give the shadow tree its own storage: either (a) proper: real shadow-root subtree + flattened-tree layout in vendor/blitz-dom (layout children of a host = shadow root children with slot assignment; unslotted light children generate no boxes), or (b) interim inside the current design: tag native children of a shadow host as `light` or `shadow` (Set of node ids per host) and (1) make JS accessors on host/shadowRoot (childNodes, children, firstChild, lastChild, next/previousSibling, firstElementChild, innerHTML, textContent, append/prepend/insertAdjacentHTML, removeChild/replaceChild, querySelector*) filter by that tag, (2) make document-level queries (getElementById, querySelectorAll, getElementsBy*, isConnected, getRootNode, contains, compareDocumentPosition) exclude `shadow` nodes and include `light` nodes, (3) hide unslotted light nodes from layout with a native 'not rendered' flag (Chromium does not render them either) and render slotted ones through the slot as today. compareDocumentPosition(host, shadowNode) must return DISCONNECTED|IMPLEMENTATION_SPECIFIC|(PRECEDING or FOLLOWING) = 37/35. Add tests to crates/script/js/test and a WPT dom/nodes shadow-dom subset.

rootCauses.title: The engine claims Chrome 140 but is missing the APIs the challenge fingerprints (WebGL, OffscreenCanvas, AudioContext, window.chrome, RTCPeerConnection, speechSynthesis, ...) and SVG text metrics are zero
rootCauses.area: crates/script/js/40_webapi.js + 90_bootstrap.js (navigator surface, window.chrome, Notification, matchMedia), new JS/natives for WebGL/OffscreenCanvas/AudioContext/RTCPeerConnection/speechSynthesis/trustedTypes, crates/script/src (canvas natives), vendor/blitz-dom (SVG <text> layout for getBBox/getComputedTextLength/getExtentOfChar)
rootCauses.mechanism: The Turnstile iframe runs a fixed fingerprint program and ships the result to Cloudflare (POST .../fo/... body ~86 KB in Chromium). Chromium's API footprint of that iframe (instr.js, iframe_api.txt) and a per-API existence probe show Sharko lacks: window.chrome (undefined; Chromium: object{loadTimes,csi,app}), WebGLRenderingContext/WebGL2RenderingContext (getContext('webgl'|'webgl2') === null; the challenge reads getParameter (incl. UNMASKED_VENDOR/RENDERER), getSupportedExtensions, getShaderPrecisionFormat, readPixels of a drawn triangle on an OffscreenCanvas), OffscreenCanvas + OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D (measureText, fillText, getImageData, transferToImageBitmap), AudioContext/OfflineAudioContext (renders an oscillator+dynamics-compressor and hashes getChannelData), RTCPeerConnection (createDataChannel/createOffer/setLocalDescription: local ICE), speechSynthesis.getVoices, navigator.mediaDevices/mediaCapabilities/credentials/keyboard/serviceWorker/gpu/userActivation/etc. (Navigator.prototype has 41 own names vs 80 in Chromium and starts with `constructor,userAgent,...` instead of Chrome's `vendorSub,productSub,vendor,maxTouchPoints,...` order), trustedTypes (the iframe's CSP is `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` and the challenge calls trustedTypes.createPolicy('default'/'QulO1')), CacheStorage/indexedDB, SharedWorker, MediaSource/canPlayType (all '' in Sharko), Notification.permission ('denied' vs 'default'), `typeof document.all` ('object' vs 'undefined'), matchMedia (color-gamut: srgb, display-mode: browser false), CSS.supports (container-type, accent-color, text-wrap false), an about:blank iframe reports location.href = parent URL and readyState 'interactive' (Chromium about:blank/'complete'), Intl default locale en-US vs navigator.language de-DE, and SVG text metrics: getBBox()/getComputedTextLength()/getExtentOfChar() return 0 or bogus (-20,-6,0,0 vs 32,18,76.9,17) although the challenge measures SVG <text> in the blank iframe. Most of these are feature-detected by the VM (no exception, the calls just do not happen), so they do not raise errors but make the report differ from every real Chrome and can be what makes Cloudflare refuse to auto-pass; which of them Cloudflare's server weighs cannot be observed from the client (see notes).
evidence: probe_env.js run in both browsers (fingerprint-api-gaps/env_chromium.json vs env_sharko.json): webgl/webgl2 null vs ctx; offscreen undefined vs function; audio undefined vs function/function; rtc undefined vs function; speech undefined vs object:0; trustedTypes undefined vs object; mediaDevices undefined vs object; chrome undefined vs object:loadTimes,csi,app; navProtoKeys 41 vs 80; canPlay '' vs 'probably'; svgBBox '-20|-6|0|0|0' vs '32|18|76.875|17|76.875'; notif denied vs default; doc.all object vs undefined; iframeBlank parent URL/'interactive' vs about:blank/'complete'.

probe_exist_run.js: 171 API members touched by the challenge in Chromium (touched_all.json, 945 members) are absent in Sharko, e.g. WebGL2RenderingContext.*, OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D.*, RTCPeerConnection.*, SpeechSynthesis.getVoices, TrustedTypePolicyFactory.createPolicy, AudioBuffer.getChannelData, ~40 Navigator members (fingerprint-api-gaps/exist_sharko.json).

Ordered trace diff: Chromium's iframe executes ~1786 traced calls, Sharko ~1401; the missing ones are precisely TrustedTypePolicy.*, SpeechSynthesis.getVoices, RTCPeerConnection.*, BaseAudioContext.*/OfflineAudioContext.startRendering, NavigatorUAData.getHighEntropyValues path, OffscreenCanvas.getContext('webgl'/'webgl2'/'2d') and WebGL2RenderingContext.getParameter/getInternalformatParameter.

Stubbing speechSynthesis, trustedTypes and RTCPeerConnection in the injected prelude did NOT remove any of the reported TypeErrors, i.e. these gaps are fingerprint differences, not the source of the exceptions.

repro.expected: Chromium: node chrome.js file://.../blank.html --eval="$(cat probe_env.js)" -> values in env_chromium.json
repro.actual: Sharko: target/profiling/browser --headless --eval="$(cat probe_env.js)" file://.../blank.html -> env_sharko.json (diff listed in the evidence)

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high for bot-management sites (Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, hCaptcha/reCAPTCHA all fingerprint WebGL/Audio/Canvas/navigator); medium otherwise (many sites feature-detect WebGL/Audio and degrade).
rootCauses.fixSketch: Priority order for a challenge that scores 'looks like Chrome 140 on Windows': (1) window.chrome = {loadTimes, csi, app, runtime absent for non-extension pages} with native-looking functions; Notification.permission 'default'; document.all typeof undefined (IsHTMLDDA); reorder/complete Navigator.prototype accessors to Chrome's order and add the missing ones as plausible objects (mediaDevices, mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo, credentials, keyboard, serviceWorker (container stub), userActivation, storage.estimate, permissions, gpu = undefined is fine on non-secure contexts), keep getters native-looking (Function.prototype.toString -> `function get vendor() { [native code] }`). (2) WebGL: implement getContext('webgl'|'webgl2'|'experimental-webgl') on HTMLCanvasElement and OffscreenCanvas returning a context object whose getParameter returns plausible ANGLE values (VENDOR 'WebKit', RENDERER 'WebKit WebGL', VERSION 'WebGL 1.0 (OpenGL ES 2.0 Chromium)', SHADING_LANGUAGE_VERSION, MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE 16384, MAX_VERTEX_ATTRIBS 16, MAX_VIEWPORT_DIMS [32767,32767], ALIASED_*_RANGE, etc.), getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info') with UNMASKED_VENDOR_WEBGL 'Google Inc. (NVIDIA)' / UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL 'ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce ..., Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0)', getSupportedExtensions (Chrome's list), getShaderPrecisionFormat ({rangeMin:127,rangeMax:127,precision:23} for FLOAT highp), getContextAttributes, drawingBufferWidth/Height, createShader/compileShader/getShaderParameter(COMPILE_STATUS true)/createProgram/linkProgram/getProgramParameter(LINK_STATUS true)/createBuffer/bufferData/vertexAttribPointer/drawArrays/readPixels (a software rasteriser for the challenge's triangle, or deterministic pixel data), createFramebuffer/createRenderbuffer/checkFramebufferStatus (=FRAMEBUFFER_COMPLETE), getInternalformatParameter for WebGL2. Minimum that satisfies fingerprint scripts: everything listed above without throwing; returning canvas-consistent non-null objects matters more than pixel exactness. (3) OffscreenCanvas (2d + webgl, transferToImageBitmap, convertToBlob) reusing the canvas 2D natives, ImageBitmap. (4) AudioContext/OfflineAudioContext: createOscillator/createDynamicsCompressor/connect/start/startRendering with a deterministic float buffer. (5) RTCPeerConnection stub (createDataChannel, createOffer/setLocalDescription resolving, onicecandidate never firing or firing a host candidate, close), speechSynthesis.getVoices() -> [], trustedTypes (createPolicy returning identity policy, isHTML/isScript...). (6) SVG text layout in vendor/blitz-dom: getBBox/getComputedTextLength/getExtentOfChar/getStartPositionOfChar from the shaped text runs. (7) about:blank iframes: location.href 'about:blank', readyState 'complete' synchronously. (8) matchMedia color-gamut/display-mode, CSS.supports for container-type/accent-color/text-wrap, canPlayType/MediaSource.isTypeSupported for common codecs, Intl default locale from navigator.language.

rootCauses.title: In the sandbox even Chromium cannot pass the challenge (brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com is blocked by the proxy and the flow ends in interactiveBegin), so pass/fail cannot be verified here
rootCauses.area: verification only (Windows CI run / unproxied network)
rootCauses.mechanism: Through the sandbox proxy Chromium (Playwright, same UA) stays on 'Nur einen Moment...' for leo.org, gutefrage.net, codepen.io, medium.com and udemy.com for 25 s, exactly like Sharko: the challenge iframe requests https://brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform/h/b/i/... which the proxy answers with CONNECT 502 (ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED in Chromium, ERR_CONNECTION_FAILED in Sharko), the challenge emits the postMessage event `interactiveBegin` in both browsers, and datacenter egress plus the proxy's TLS/HTTP2 fingerprint probably lowers the trust score. Plain curl through the proxy gets the hard 'Sorry, you have been blocked' page. The request sequence (orchestrate chl_page -> POST fo -> turnstile iframe -> POST fo -> pat 401 -> ci image -> final POST fo of ~86 KB) is identical in both browsers; the only Sharko-only requests are the two POST .../eb/.../chl_api_m error beacons and a larger final fo body (94-97 KB vs 86 KB). No cf_clearance cookie appears in either browser here (Sharko document.cookie stays empty; `cf_chl_rc_ni=6` is set only in some runs). The NaN console lines are NOT errors: they are the challenge's devtools-detection console trap (console.log('%c%d', 'font-size:0;color:transparent', NaN) etc.), Chromium prints the same lines.
evidence: chrome.js/trace.js on leo.org, gutefrage.net, codepen.io, medium.com, udemy.com: title stays 'Nur einen Moment...', document.cookie empty after 25 s.
mitm log: `#9 tunnel error CONNECT 502` for brunhild.challenges.cloudflare.com in every run (Sharko and Chromium).
Chromium behind the same MITM proxy + same prelude: events init, requestExtraParams, translationInit, meow/food x13, interactiveBegin - identical event stream to Sharko (postMessage log).

repro.expected: Windows CI (no proxy): Chromium reaches the real site
repro.actual: sandbox: Chromium also stays on the interstitial

rootCauses.fixSketch: Use the console-free success criteria that ARE observable in the sandbox after fixing the engine: (1) no `ERR-STRINGIFY`/`WINERR` lines from the turnstile iframe and zero POST .../eb/.../chl_api_m requests when running scratchpad/rc/cf-challenge/runm.sh with mitm/prelude1.js (Chromium: 0/0), (2) the ordered API trace of the iframe (prelude4) has no divergence except the Trusted-Types/WebGL-family calls that are implemented, (3) then confirm cf_clearance on the Windows CI run (tools/sitediff without proxy).

notes: How the mechanism was found: a logging/rewriting MITM proxy (scratchpad/rc/cf-challenge/mitm/proxy.js; Sharko gets HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:38111 and SHARKO_EXTRA_CA=mitm/ca.pem, upstream is the sandbox proxy over HTTP/2 so Cloudflare still serves the JS challenge; an HTTP/1.1 upstream gets the hard block page) injects preludes into every HTML document (the challenge iframe's CSP nonce is reused) so the challenge's own error reporter (JSON.stringify(Error, ownPropertyNames) -> POST /eb/.../chl_api_m) and an ordered DOM/Web API call trace can be observed in Sharko and in Chromium behind the same proxy. Result: Sharko is the only one reporting errors, always the same two on all 11 affected sites checked (leo.org, codepen.io, gutefrage.net, medium.com run three times each): (a) `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'replaceChild')` = root cause cross-realm-adopt-by-copy (fully explained, minimal repro), (b) `TypeError: <reg> is not a function` = a VM call on an undefined value. (b) is only PARTLY explained: in unpatched runs the undefined value is querySelectorAll('#crERV20')[0] followed by .insertAdjacentHTML (CFGET-ONUNDEF key=insertAdjacentHTML), caused by shadow-host-light-dom-lost; with body.attachShadow redirected to a child div (shim in mitm/prelude8/12/13.js) that instance disappears but a `Wk is not a function` from the plain call handler still occurs; I could not identify its callee (the VM keeps callees in registers; the served script is re-obfuscated per request so a static patch did not catch that call form). Ruled out as the source of the exceptions: missing speechSynthesis, trustedTypes, RTCPeerConnection (stubbed, errors unchanged), the console NaN lines, `Timezone "UTC" not found` (Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone is 'UTC' and works), plain insertAdjacentHTML on an unknown element, template.content/importNode, iframe contentDocument in the same realm, blob Workers (Worker+Blob URL work). Next step for whoever fixes (b): re-run `mitm/start.sh LOG mitm/prelude12.js mitm/patch_vm2.js; ./runm.sh https://www.leo.org/ out` after fixing the two root causes above and check whether `Wk/aN/WB is not a function` remains; if it does, extend mitm/patch_vm2.js to patch the register-call handler (the function whose body contains `Wk=Wn[Wk^WC],We!==0){`) to dump the previous VM property-get names. Possibly relevant remaining differences to check first: Navigator.getBattery/getGamepads results, navigator.userAgentData.getHighEntropyValues shape, OffscreenCanvas/AudioContext absence when the VM does NOT feature-detect. The larger final fo POST (94-97 KB vs 86 KB in Chromium) is the error text plus different probe results. Other observations for other clusters: indexedDB/caches are undefined in the frames of this page (window.indexedDB undefined in the challenge iframe and in file:// pages), SharedWorker undefined, `Element.prototype.attachShadow` on <body> is allowed (Chromium allows it too), document.readyState is 'interactive' when --eval runs on some file:// pages. mediamarkt/saturn/rewe/doctolib show custom Cloudflare Turnstile wrappers ("Lieber Besucher, Das ging uns leider zu schnell", "Zeig uns, dass du ein Mensch bist") that embed the same turnstile iframe, so the same causes apply; chat.openai.com shows an empty text (challenge iframe only) and was not analysed separately. Tools and traces are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/cf-challenge/ (README-tools.txt).
